newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on frost concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on frost concerns.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed higher on concerns about several outlooks for a frost in key areas of the Midwest as early as September 21, traders said.

"Obviously the frost word scared people to death this morning and that supported breaks," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co. "The concern is a frost could halt the growing season and there are a couple of people talking about frost between September 21 and September 24."
A cold front could bring freezing temperatures from Kansas City to Chicago by September 24, said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster with Weather Express Inc.
"Based on today's MRF (medium range forecast), I'm forecasting a 60 to 70 percent probability of there being a freeze north of I-80 (Interstate 80), 80 percent chance for Minnesota," Gesser said.
Soybeans ended the day near the session highs which were set late with technical buy stops coupled with a fund-related surge in soyoil contributing to the advances.
"Higher lows, higher highs and what you get is a higher close," Cermak said.
Soybeans closed 4-1/4 to 10-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with September up 4-1/4 at $8.35-3/4.
November closed 9-1/2 cents per bushel higher at $9.14-1/2.
The chart-based demand surfaced in late trading when November breached Wednesday's high of $8.12-1/2. Buy-stops were implemented at that level.
The late demand in soyoil was tied to purchases from Griffin Trading and Rosenthal Collins, the traders said.
Soybean volume was estimated at 58,000 contracts, down from 72,701 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.

In the soyben options pit Term Commodities bought 500 November $7.75 puts at 8-3/4 cents, Cargill Investor Services bought 400 November $7.50 puts at 3-1/2 to 3-3/8 cents and Lee B. Stern and Co bought 300 January $8.50 calls at 21-1/2 to 21 cents, the traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 28,000 contracts, down from 37,098 Wednesday.
